howTo: Enter the linear spring stiffness k in N/m (e.g. 500 N/m).
Enter the maximum displacement x_max in millimetres (mm).
Specify the number of evaluation points (steps ≥ 2).
Review the resulting force–displacement curve and numerical step-by-step table based on Hooke's Law.
formula: F = k · x | x [m] = x_mm / 1000 | Step size = x_max / (steps − 1)

examples.title: Return spring with 6 evaluation steps
examples.description: A spring with stiffness k = 500 N/m compressed up to 20 mm across 6 equally spaced points.
notes: Step interval = 20 mm / (6 - 1) = 4 mm per point.

examples.title: Industrial compression spring
examples.description: A heavy-duty compression spring with k = 8 000 N/m compressed up to 50 mm evaluated over 11 steps.
notes: Linear Hooke's Law assumption requires operating strictly below the spring solid height.

commonMistakes: Entering displacement in millimetres while treating stiffness as N/mm instead of N/m.
Exceeding the physical solid height or maximum allowable deflection of the spring.
Applying linear Hooke's Law to progressive-rate or dual-rate non-linear springs.
assumptions: Ideal linear elastic behaviour (Hooke's Law) over the entire displacement range.
Initial preload at zero displacement is assumed to be zero.
Hysteresis, temperature degradation, and damping are not modelled.
